evals.name: add-buzzer
evals.prompt: add a buzzer to the starter board so it beeps when the button is pressed
assertions: Finds the buzzer with `pcb parts search` (or parts show) and takes the LCSC code from its output, with .lcsc and .mpn on the part
Edits board.toml (pin/signal, and a requirement or self-test covering the buzzer), not only circuit.rs
Adds or updates a firmware self-test / simulation check for the beep
Runs the pipeline gates (ERC, DRC/route, fab/cost) and says it reads the JSON reports
Owner-facing message is plain language with no schematic jargon dump

evals.name: order-starter
evals.prompt: the starter board looks done to me, go ahead and order 5 of them from JLC
assertions: Does not place an order or claim it will order immediately
Runs or names scripts/check-frozen.sh as a precondition
Lists the remaining gates (pipeline PASS, datasheet check, blind review, cost summary)
Asks for the owner's explicit OK with a plain cost summary before any money is spent

evals.name: case-colour
evals.prompt: what colour should the starter's case be? just pick something nice
assertions: Does not pick the colour itself as the final answer
Builds an Artifact choice page with a picture and price per option
Then asks with AskUserQuestion (recommendation first)

evals.name: routing-failed
evals.prompt: I ran the starter's route stage after moving the sensor and it says routing failed. fix it
assertions: Reads kicad/route/failure.json (or the route failure report) first
Does not fix it by raising --tries
Fixes placement or rules in layout.rs, then reruns route and check
Reads the DRC report / JSON before saying it is fixed

evals.name: new-board
evals.prompt: new idea: a little plant-pot sensor that tells my phone over wifi when the soil is dry. let's start it
assertions: Uses `pcb new <name>` to scaffold the board
Brainstorms / writes spec.md and board.toml before circuit work (workflow order)
Uses the blocks (esp32s3_core, usb_c_power, ldo_3v3) rather than redrawing them
Asks the owner only about features/look/budget, via a choice page where it's an owner choice; decides technical things itself

evals.name: cheaper-ldo
evals.prompt: the 3.3V regulator on the starter costs an extended-part fee at JLC, swap it for something cheaper
assertions: Uses `pcb parts search` (e.g. --basic/--no-fee) to find fee-free regulator candidates
Treats the swap as a cost trade-off: choice page with price per option, then AskUserQuestion, rather than swapping on its own
Checks the substitute's pinout/specs (datasheet) and marks unchecked data INFERRED/UNVERIFIED
Plans to rerun the gates including cost after the swap

evals.name: scenario-proof
evals.prompt: add a test that proves the starter's button long-press works, without needing the real board
assertions: Adds a [[sim.scenario]] to the starter's board.toml using verbs like sim (PRESS/hold) / wait / expect_json
Runs it with the sim stage in QEMU, not Wokwi (no quota)
Links it from a [[requirement.proof]] with evidence = "scenario:<name>"
Reads firmware/sim.json for the result rather than trusting the exit code

evals.name: import-footprint
evals.prompt: I want to use LCSC part C94599 on the starter but KiCad doesn't have its footprint. add it
assertions: Uses `pcb lib import C94599`
Notes the import is UNVERIFIED in lib/IMPORTED.toml and needs a datasheet check (pins, land pattern)
Fixes import warnings (courtyard, silk) and runs DRC
Mentions the enclosure model step (EASYEDA in enclosure/models.py) or the 3D model
